title: LaMUX: Optimized Logic-Gate-Enabled High-Performance Microfluidic Multiplexer Design
problem: Existing microfluidic multiplexer designs have limited coding capacities, resulting in significant area overhead and excessive chip-to-world interface connections as the number of microvalves increases to meet increasingly complex experimental demands.
motivation: Flow-based microfluidic biochips require growing numbers of microvalves for complex biochemical experiments, necessitating more efficient multiplexing solutions to control device actuation.
method: The approach designs a new gate structure for the multiplexer (the control switch that routes fluids) and combines it with mixed coding—using different encoding strategies together to represent more control options in the same physical space. This gate-and-coding combination reduces overhead: you can control more microfluidic valves without needing extra input connections. The authors created LaMUX, an automated tool that designs these mixed-coding multiplexers for pneumatically-driven microfluidic systems (systems using compressed air to push fluids through channels).
key_novelty: Pairing a new gate structure with mixed coding (combining different encoding strategies) to pack more microfluidic-valve control into fewer pneumatic connections and valves.
contributions: Novel gate structure for modifying microfluidic MUX architecture
Mixed coding strategy achieving maximum coding capacity
LaMUX synthesis tool for automated design of optimized multiplexers
Substantial reduction in pneumatic controllers and microvalves usage compared to existing MUX designs
